sources.title: Understanding biodiversity net gain
sources.publisher: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
sources.verified_claim: DEFRA states mandatory BNG rules and records changes due to take effect on 6 August 2026, including an exemption for developments of 0.2 hectares or below. Because 6 August is future-dated relative to this 24 July 2026 batch, the announced change is retained as future policy and not treated as already effective.

sources.title: Biodiversity net gain: what local planning authorities should do
sources.publisher: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
sources.verified_claim: DEFRA sets out LPA checks for planning applications, biodiversity gain plans and monitoring. The page also records the future 6 August 2026 small-development change, which is not treated as current law before that date.

sources.title: What you can count towards a development’s biodiversity net gain
sources.publisher: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
sources.verified_claim: DEFRA explains which habitat creation or enhancement measures can count toward a development's BNG and records the 2 November 2026 NSIP start date. These rules require proposal-specific habitat evidence and do not prove a sample parcel's biodiversity value.

sources.title: Biodiversity Net Gain
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's planning page explains local BNG validation expectations, exemptions, securing delivery and proposed monitoring/enforcement. The page includes draft local guidance, so draft status is retained and no exact parcel metric is inferred.

sources.title: Climate change and biodiversity
sources.verified_claim: Enfield links its Biodiversity Action Plan and adopted Blue and Green Strategy to protection, management and expansion of blue-green infrastructure and to planning for new development; borough strategy is not parcel-level habitat evidence.

sources.title: Biodiversity Net Gain
sources.verified_claim: Havering explains mandatory 10% BNG, minimum 30-year securing and planning validation information, while stressing that BNG does not replace existing protected-site, habitat or species controls. Exact applicability remains proposal-specific.

sources.title: Biodiversity in Lambeth
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's biodiversity page describes local habitats, SINCs and the new 2026 Pollinator Action Plan alongside older biodiversity-plan material. Strategy and designation context is not an exact parcel intersection.

sources.title: Submit or pay for a planning application
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth states that where a Section 106 obligation secures post-approval BNG, long-term monitoring fees over 30 years may be included and assessed case by case. A monitoring fee route does not establish BNG applicability or outcome for the sample parcel.
